body.heading: Find a trail
paragraphs: On a dry day, look along a path or near a wall for a line of busy ants. They often walk in a long line, like a tiny train on an invisible track.
The ants are following a smell trail that other ants left behind. The smell tells them: this way to food, this way home.

body.heading: Watch the workers
paragraphs: Follow the trail with your eyes. Where does it start? Where does it end? Some ants may carry crumbs or bits of leaf bigger than themselves.
Ants are very strong for their size. A crumb to an ant is like a whole loaf of bread to you. Watch how they pass each other without bumping.

body.heading: A tiny test
paragraphs: Ask your adult to place a small leaf near the trail, not on it. Watch whether the ants explore it or march straight past.
When you finish, leave the trail exactly as you found it. The ants still have a busy day of work to do.

takeaway: Ants follow smell trails in long lines, and careful watching shows you their whole busy world.
materials: A magnifying glass if you have one
safetyNotes: Never touch ants or their nests, and never block their path with your hands. Some ants can bite, so keep fingers away.
screenFreeExtension: Draw a map of the ant trail at home and add the places the ants visited, like a treasure map.
